parts.final_form: both cases (n even, n odd) treated algebraically, with conclusion
parts.ms: Trying a few values scores 0. M1 one case n = 2k or 2k + 1 substituted; M1 both cases; A1 both simplified with at least one shown even (20k² + 22k + 18, 20k² + 2k + 12); A1 factor 2 extracted in both and full conclusion, variable other than n. "Logic" approaches max M1M1A0A0 (MS p.23)

parts.ask: Show that the statement "(n + 1)³ − n³ is prime for all n ∈ ℕ" is false
parts.final_form: a counter-example with the value shown not prime, plus a conclusion
parts.ms: M1 search for a counter-example (e.g. n = 1, 2, 3 give primes); A1 a counter-example with reason and conclusion, e.g. n = 5: 6³ − 5³ = 91 = 7 × 13, so the statement is not true. Purely algebraic approaches score 0 (MS p.11)

parts.ask: A(1, 0), B(3, −10), C(7, −6) lie on a circle: prove that AB is a diameter
parts.final_form: proof (e.g. AC ⟂ BC so angle ACB = 90°, angle in a semicircle) with a conclusion
parts.ms: Way 1: M1 a gradient AC or BC; A1 m_AC = −1, m_BC = 1; dM1A1 product −1; A1 angle ACB = 90° so AB is a diameter, conclusion with no errors. Way 2: lengths, AB² = 104 = 72 + 32 (Pythagoras). Way 3: midpoint M of AB with MA = MC (MS pp.11–13)

parts.final_form: decreasing exponential curve through (0, 1) (or (0, k)) approaching the t-axis without crossing it; may extend left of the N-axis
parts.ms: M1 correct shape (decreasing, no turning points) through a point on the positive vertical axis; A1 intercept 1 (or k), asymptote to the t-axis, not crossing below it (MS p.22)

parts.ask: Half-life 5700 years: show λ = 0.999878 to 6 decimal places
parts.final_form: given value to 6 d.p. from λ⁵⁷⁰⁰ = 1/2
parts.ms: M1 (1/2)k = kλ⁵⁷⁰⁰ ⇒ λ⁵⁷⁰⁰ = 1/2; A1* λ = (1/2)^(1/5700) = 0.999878 with the fractional-root step seen (logs route allowed; 5699 for 5700 scores M1A0). Alt: substitute 0.9998775 and 0.9998785 and conclude (MS pp.22–23)

parts.ask: Item A: k = 15 g, age 3250 years: calculate the predicted amount now
parts.ms: M1 N = 15 × 0.999878³²⁵⁰ (3249 allowed; a less accurate λ such as 0.9999 condoned for M1); A1 awrt 10.1 (grams). Answer only can score both marks (MS pp.22–23)

parts.ask: Item B: 25 g initially, 18 g now: use algebra to find its age
parts.final_form: nearest 100 years; logarithms used (algebraic method required)
parts.ms: B1 18 = 25 × 0.999878ᵗ (given λ or better; 0.9999 is B0); M1 correct log work to make t the subject; A1 2700 (from 2692.49…; "27 hundred" accepted) (MS pp.22–23)

parts.ask: Circle C centre X(3, 5), radius r; line l: y = 2x + k: show they intersect when 5x² + (4k − 26)x + k² − 10k + 34 − r² = 0
parts.ms: M1 substitute y = 2x + k into (x − 3)² + (y − 5)² = r²; dM1 expand and collect x², x terms; A1* given equation (MS p.24)

parts.ask: Given l is a tangent to C, show 5r² = (k + p)², p to be found
parts.ms: M1 b² − 4ac = 0 for the quadratic in (a); M1 expand to 5r² = …; A1 5r² = k² + 2k + 1 = (k + 1)², p = 1. Way 2: radius BX gradient −1/2, find B and use distance BX = r (MS p.24)

parts.ask: l meets the y-axis at A and touches C at B (Figure 2); AB = 2r: find k
parts.final_form: value of k consistent with Figure 2 (radius ⟂ tangent, Pythagoras AX² = AB² + r²)
parts.ms: M1 right angle at B: AB² + r² = XA² = 3² + (5 − k)²; M1 AB² = 4r² so XA² = 5r²; A1 5r² = 9 + (5 − k)²; M1 equate with (k + 1)²; dM1 12k = 33; A1 k = 11/4 (MS p.24)

parts.ask: a, b, c positive integers with c = b + 2 and a + b + c = 10: prove by exhaustion that the product abc is always even (table offered)
parts.final_form: every valid case listed (b = 1, 2, 3) with its product, other cases excluded, and a conclusion
parts.ms: B1 one correct row (a, b, c) = (6,1,3), (4,2,4) or (2,3,5); M1 product abc for at least 2 valid combinations; A1* all three valid combinations with correct products, no other combinations, and a (minimal) conclusion. Algebraic route a = 8 − 2b, abc = 2(4 − b)b(b + 2) accepted; "−2b³ + 4b² + 16b which is even" alone is "not sufficient" (MS p.7)
parts.er: Poorly answered, many blanks; some used c = b − 2, ignored that a, b, c are positive, or found the sum instead of the "product"; many with three correct rows gave no conclusion; algebraic attempts long-winded and error-prone (ER p.3)

parts.ask: f(x) = (2 − kx)⁵; remainder when f(x) is divided by (4x − 5) is 243/32: show that k = 2/5
parts.final_form: given value; must take the 5th root of 243/32 (not just state k)
parts.ms: M1 f(5/4) = 243/32 and take the 5th root to make k the subject; A1* k = 2/5 with sufficient working, minimum (2 − 5k/4)⁵ = 243/32 ⇒ 2 − 5k/4 = 3/2 ⇒ k = 2/5. Verification route: evaluate 2 − kx with k = 2/5, x = 5/4 and conclude (MS p.8)
parts.er: Remainder theorem known but working often insufficient; 4/5 substituted in error; long division or expanding attempted; verifiers rarely concluded (ER p.3)

parts.ask: First three terms, ascending powers of x, of the binomial expansion of (2 − 2x/5)⁵, each term simplest form
parts.ms: M1 correct binomial coefficient with correct power of 2 and of ±2x/5 for the x or x² term; A1 −32x or +(64/5)x²; A1 32 − 32x + (64/5)x² (12.8 allowed); extra terms ignored but no isw on the final answer (MS pp.8–9)
parts.er: Sign slips from using +2x/5; some spoiled a correct expansion by multiplying through by 5 (ER p.3)

parts.ask: Using part (b), making the method clear, find the gradient of C where x = 0
parts.final_form: a value obtained by differentiating the expansion
parts.ms: M1 differentiate their expansion and substitute x = 0; A1ft −32 (ft q from p + qx + rx²) (MS pp.8–9)
parts.er: Some differentiated the original f(x) instead of using (b); commonest error was substituting x = 0 into f(x) (ER p.3)

parts.ask: Model w = logₐ(t + 5) − logₐ4 (2 ≤ t ≤ 18); w = 10 when t = 3: show a = 1.072 to 3 d.p.
parts.final_form: given value; show a = 2^(1/10) (or ¹⁰√2) before awrt 1.072
parts.ms: M1 substitute and use the subtraction law to reach logₐ2 = 10; M1 a¹⁰ = 2; A1* a = 2^(1/10) = 1.07177… shown. "False solutions": logₐ8 − logₐ4 written as logₐ8/logₐ4 then reaching a¹⁰ = 2 scores M0M1A0; 8 log a/4 log a manipulation scores 0 (MS p.11)

parts.ms: M1 subtraction law to w = log₁.₀₇₂((t + 5)/4); M1 remove log, 1.072ʷ = f(t), make t subject; A1 t = 4 × 1.072ʷ − 5. Alt: t = 1.072^(w + log₁.₀₇₂4) − 5 (MS pp.11–12)
parts.er: Errors: log(t + 5) split as log t + log 5; 4(1.072ʷ) "simplified" to 4.288ʷ; alternative method users often used a rounded log 4 value and lost the A1 (ER p.4)

parts.ask: Find t when w = 15, to 3 s.f.
parts.ms: M1 substitute w = 15 into their equation or the original; A1 awrt 6.35 (full-accuracy a gives 6.3137… and scores A0) (MS p.12)

parts.final_form: given equation, no errors; arguments (θ) kept throughout
parts.ms: M1 tan θ = sin θ/cos θ to reach sine and cosine only; M1 sin²θ + cos²θ = 1 to get a quadratic in sine; A1* printed equation with no errors (one notational slip condoned in working, printed answer must be correct) (MS p.13)

parts.final_form: all four solutions in radians (awrt −1.13, −0.438, 0.225, 1.35), no extras in range
parts.ms: M1 solve the quadratic (calculator allowed); A1 sin 2x = (−1 ± √13)/6 (awrt 0.43, −0.77); M1 arcsin of a root then divide by 2; A1 any two of −1.13, −0.438, 0.225, 1.35; A1 all four and no others. Degrees: SC max 7/8 (MS p.13)
